documents.title: Using Generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) Technology at the University at Buffalo
documents.stance_why: The guidance sets no default allow or ban; it says 'Students must use AI tools in accordance with their instructor's guidance' and is mainly about data privacy, ethics and responsible use, so the decision is handed to instructors (delegates).
documents.summary: UBIT guidance, established January 2024, on responsible use of generative AI across UB. It covers data privacy (no Category 1 or 2 data in uncontracted tools), ethics, IP, verifying output, and software review, and leaves classroom use to instructors and the academic integrity policy.

documents.unit: Department of Computer Science and Engineering
documents.title: CSE Generative AI Policy
documents.stance_why: The policy acknowledges useful AI roles ('communicate in an unfamiliar language', 'brainstorming') but requires authors to own content and disclose AI use, 'including ... editing for grammar'; AI is allowed with conditions of disclosure and responsibility (permit). It covers only theses and scholarly writing.
documents.summary: A short departmental policy on generative AI in theses, capstone documents and other scholarly writing. It weighs benefits against risks and sets three baseline expectations: authors are responsible for content, must disclose provenance including AI use, and must own the work.

units.why: CSE 'recognizes that Generative AI tools can help students communicate in an unfamiliar language' and have uses 'when brainstorming'; these are permitted uses. P15 (brainstorming) is chosen, P18 (prose) is noted.

units.fit_note: Also covers language assistance and building temporary scaffolds, not only brainstorming.
